segments.text: When the gods vanished, the people in charge of the Remosan Empire set themselves to fixing things, and they were the wrong people for the job. They were the innocent children of the Shining Age. They had never seen a wound that didn't close or a spell that failed. War, to them, was a kind of strenuous theater. Death was a story you told at dinner. The idea that an action could have a consequence which then stayed was not something their education had prepared them for.

And so they reached for the tools. The damage of the Sundering was severe but not yet total. The Imperial Highways still ran from coast to coast and healed themselves overnight. Grain still moved between provinces. The Gyre-Stones still stood across the empire, each holding its patch of the world steady. What was missing was the maintenance the gods had been quietly performing, and the empire's generals and archmages set themselves to replicate it.

They had the old records and the leftover instruments, sometimes even vague memories of how these were once used. They had no idea what they were doing. They didn't even have the framework for understanding that their ignorance was dangerous.

The trouble was that they didn't agree on what needed restoring, or how. The Shining Age had as many priesthoods as it had gods, each with its own methods and records, and while the gods were present the differences hadn't mattered. After the Sundering they mattered enormously. Every surviving tradition believed it held the correct approach to a job none of their patrons had ever done alone, and none of them were willing to give an inch to the others.

The Age of Silence lasted longer than anyone expected. The damage scaled with the tools. The gods had left behind an entire apparatus of creation: forges, instruments, weapons, arcane infrastructure built to operate on a divine scale. Mortals now held all of it, understood very little of it, and had no way to test their ideas at anything less than full power. Mages reached for ruinous and experimental schools of magic, and were quick to weaponize them.

The results irradiated whole populations and twisted entire villages into the crystalline Varn. Elsewhere the Kelara Peaks tore loose from the continent and rose into the upper air, and are still there. When human soldiers proved too fragile for terrain that no longer behaved, the imperial bio-forges began producing the Or-Rack, designed from the start to survive what men could not.

As famine and arcane radiation hollowed the labor base, the administration turned to the Graith: given the empire's last clear instructions, set to maintain the infrastructure no living workforce could.

None of it worked. Even the names of the priesthoods and the specifics of their disagreements have not survived. Many of the Soft Zones and Rifts on the modern map are the work of what later ages called the Witch Wars.

They are artillery craters from when humanity broke the world trying to force it back into shape. By the end, the empire was still there in name, but it had used itself up. What came next happened because it no longer had the authority to hold the provinces together.
